summary: SB 8, titled the Texas Women's Privacy Act, amends Chapter 3002 of the Texas Government Code to regulate the designation and use of certain spaces and facilities according to sex. It requires political subdivisions and state agencies to designate multiple-occupancy private spaces for use exclusively by individuals of one sex and prohibits opposite-sex individuals from using them without specific exceptions (custody, maintenance, medical emergencies, accompaniment, law enforcement, safety threats, and children under 9). The Act authorizes civil penalties of $5,000 for first violations and $25,000 for subsequent violations, and creates a private civil cause of action allowing affected parties to seek declaratory and injunctive relief plus attorney's fees. The Attorney General can investigate complaints and collect penalties. The bill takes effect 91 days after the legislative session ends (2025-09-22).

summary: SB 9 amends the Texas Tax Code to revise how voter-approval tax rates are calculated for various taxing units. The bill defines three distinct formulas: special taxing units use a rate of (NO-NEW-REVENUE MAINTENANCE AND OPERATIONS RATE × 1.08) plus current debt rate; municipalities or counties with populations under 75,000 (excluding special taxing units) use (NO-NEW-REVENUE MAINTENANCE AND OPERATIONS RATE × 1.035) plus current debt rate plus unused increment rate; and other taxing units use (NO-NEW-REVENUE MAINTENANCE AND OPERATIONS RATE × 1.025[1.035]) plus current debt rate plus unused increment rate. The legislation also updates related sections regarding calculations during periods of new sales and use tax imposition and specifies that governing bodies may direct officers to calculate rates up to the lesser of specified amounts. The act takes effect January 1, 2026, and was reported engrossed on August 6, 2025.

summary: HB 242, introduced in the Texas House in 2025, amends the Government Code and Health and Safety Code to establish a statewide natural disaster alert system and flood safety requirements. The bill requires flood-risk zones, areas impacted by flooding at least once in the past century, to have outdoor warning sirens installed at two-mile intervals, equipped with water-level sensors and solar-powered backups. Local governments, counties, and municipalities must either install, maintain, and operate these sirens or jointly manage them through agreements. An additional subsection adds flood safety requirements for youth camps near rivers or lakes, mandating radio equipment in cabins and flotation devices on beds. The legislation also defines key terms and establishes testing and documentation requirements. It takes effect 91 days after the legislative session ends and was filed on July 31, 2025.
